newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: LEGAL ADVICE REVEALS DETAIL OF 10-POINT WIK PLAN

It's been revealed the Prime Minister's ten-point plan on native title allows the states and territories to extinguish native title on many forms of title, including agricultural leases. Legal advice to the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission on the plan also reveals government services affecting native title land can be provided without recognising native title. It shows pastoralists can engage in tourism without recognising native title, and that native title rights in water are severly restricted if not extinguished. It says native title rights are decreased on mining land, and that there's only one right to negotiate per project.

The advice states that under the plan States are encouraged to set up their own ways of dealing with native title claims, and all claims should be lodged by a certain date - possibly the year 2004. As well, negotiated voluntary binding agreements on native title are encouraged.

Prime Minister, John Howard, is appealing to supporters of Independent MP Pauline Hanson saying she's got no answers, and her cure would be worse than the disease. In what's been his strongest ever attack on the MP, Mr Howard has accused the member for Oxley of being sour, bitter and narrow-minded. Speaking at dinner promoting better links with Asian business, Mr Howard said Miss Hanson was wrong to seek scapegoats for society's problems. He said she was also wrong in suggesting Aborigines aren't disadvantaged.

In Melbourne thousands of visitors have had their first look at the city's new billion dollar Crown Entertainment Complex. The centre officially opened for business last night at a star-studded gala and fireworks spectacular on the Yarra River. During the evening the champagne flowed as freely as did the accolades for developer Lloyd Williams and Premier Jeff Kennett who both officially opened the complex.

A 30,000-tonne bulk carrier has run aground on Tiparra Reef -- just south of Wallaroo -- in South Australia's St Vincent Gulf. The Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre says it's understood there's no oil spillage and no structural damage to the Korean vessel, which struck gHarbour officials plan to fly over the vessel, "Western Winner", early this morning to determine whether tugs will be needed to move it.

It's been revealed a looming court case and charges including drink driving, theft, and assault, prompted a New Zealand twins Sarah and Joanne Ingham to stow away on a container ship in February. The 18 year-olds and a Malaysian crewman jumped ship in waters off north Queensland, surviving shark and crocadile infested waters and more than two weeks in rugged country. The twins were deported from Australia, and New Zealand police arrested them when their plane landed in Auckland. Their parents say the impending charges are minor and somewhat irrelevant considering the ordeal the family has been through.
